text:
Buyers assess corn quality mainly on dryness, cleanliness (freedom from trash and foreign matter), and low broken-kernel percentage, with better-quality grain commanding a higher price. Corn marketing infrastructure in Cambodia has developed significantly since the company Charoen Pokphand-Cambodia (C.P.-Cambodia / CP Foods) established operations, including collection points and processing facilities in several locations, with warehouse and drying infrastructure noted in Pailin among other areas.

Contract farming arrangements with buyers such as CP Foods can give farmers more price certainty than selling on the open spot market, and some of these arrangements include access to drying and storage infrastructure. Farmers' net returns depend on managing production costs (labour, seed, fertilizer, pesticide) against the price received, and price transparency -- knowing what fair market price to expect -- affects farmers' bargaining position when selling, whether through a contract arrangement or on the open market.
